## High-accuracy services (25 min)

### [Core] Why high accuracy needs more than broadcast ephemerides

- **Placeholder — error budget:** orbit and clock errors, signal biases, ionospheric/tropospheric delays, multipath and receiver noise.
- **Placeholder — model:** how correction quality and observation geometry map into position covariance and convergence.
- **Placeholder — comparison:** relative positioning (common-mode cancellation) versus PPP (precise products and ambiguity resolution).

### [Core] Galileo High Accuracy Service (HAS)

- **Placeholder — service architecture:** corrections generated by a ground segment and delivered through Galileo E6-B and an internet data distribution channel.
- **Placeholder — correction content:** satellite orbit and clock, plus code and phase biases; explain which observation models consume them.
- **Placeholder — performance and user algorithm:** service area, convergence, accuracy, availability, message freshness, and receiver assumptions.
- **Placeholder — board derivation:** corrected pseudorange/carrier phase and the role of signal-specific biases.

### [Core] BeiDou PPP-B2b

- **Placeholder — architecture and signal:** PPP corrections broadcast by BDS-3 satellites; contrast the broadcast link with HAS delivery.
- **Placeholder — message content:** satellite mask, orbit and clock corrections, code bias, and user-range-accuracy information.
- **Placeholder — coordinate/time references and coverage:** make datum and inter-system reference compatibility explicit when comparing with IGS products.
- **Placeholder — worked example:** apply a radial/along-track/cross-track correction and a clock correction to a broadcast state.

### [Optional depth] Other high-accuracy services and modes

- **QZSS CLAS:** regional centimetre-level corrections, with network/PPP-RTK concepts and its local service area.
- **QZSS MADOCA-PPP:** wide-area PPP corrections delivered on L6; discuss convergence and the distinction from local network RTK.
- **QZSS SLAS:** sub-metre regional augmentation; a useful contrast showing the accuracy/coverage/cost trade space below centimetre-level services.
- **RTK and PPP-RTK:** baseline differencing, ambiguity fixing, atmospheric decorrelation and network densification.
- **Commercial PPP/PPP-RTK:** use as a service-model example; avoid vendor-specific performance claims unless sourced for the lecture date.

### [Lighter view] One comparison slide

- Compare HAS, PPP-B2b, CLAS/MADOCA and RTK by correction source, delivery, coverage, convergence and hardware/network needs.
